data.title: DSMLC Annual Final Competition
data.subtitle: The DSMLC Annual Final Competition is your chance to showcase your data science and machine learning expertise, compete for top prizes, and make a lasting impact in the industry.

data.text: The Data Science and Machine Learning Club at the University of Calgary hosts an annual competition to give students an opportunity to showcase their programming and data science skills. Open to university students, it provides a platform to demonstrate their abilities using a comprehensive dataset in front of the broader community. This competition involves data science tasks including visualization, manipulation, and analysis, applying classroom concepts to real-world data.

Participation in this competition allows students to gain recognition for their achievements, build their portfolios, and make valuable connections that support their career development in data science.

points.text: With over 100+ attendees, the 2026 Final Competition was our biggest event yet! In collaboration with Enbridge, students were challenged to come up with an applicable data solution working with a Wind Farm SCADA dataset. We had Speakers from Urban systems, DAMA Calgary, Enbridge, and ATB to discuss and speak about their chosen topics.

The 2025 Competition was an immense success. With three unique categories and four highly talented speakers: Corey Yang from Urban System, Pierce Anderson from ARC Resources, Helen Ashton from AWS, and Banks Odole from SAIT, attendees gained new connections and insights.

The 2024 competition reached new heights with keynote speaker Renee Matsalla from Tacit Edge. Her discussion on data science in product management added an industry-focused perspective, making the event highly relevant for attendees.

Our inaugural competition was a resounding success, featuring sponsorship from ARC Resources and an inspiring keynote address by Dr. Xuewen Lu, who shared valuable academic insights into the field of data science.

faq.question: What is the Final Competition?
faq.answer: The Final Competition is an annual event where students showcase their skills in data science and machine learning by working on real-world datasets. It provides a platform to learn, innovate, and network with peers and industry professionals.

faq.question: Who can participate in the competition?
faq.answer: The competition is open to all students, regardless of their academic background or level of experience. Participation can be as an individual or as part of a team, depending on the year's rules.

faq.question: What are the categories of the competition?
faq.answer: Participants can compete in various categories, such as Data Visualization, Machine Learning, and Research Proposal. Each category focuses on different skill sets, offering opportunities to highlight unique talents.

faq.question: What tools or programming languages can I use?
faq.answer: Participants are free to use any programming language or software they are comfortable with. Popular tools include Python, R, Tableau, and Excel, but creativity and originality are the key factors.

faq.question: Can I use additional datasets?
faq.answer: Most competitions allow the use of supplementary datasets, as long as they are open-source and properly cited. Specific rules about additional data will be outlined in the competition guidelines.

faq.question: What are the benefits of participating?
faq.answer: The competition offers hands-on experience with real-world data, helps build your portfolio, provides networking opportunities with industry professionals, and offers the chance to win awards and recognition.

faq.question: How are submissions evaluated?
faq.answer: Submissions are typically judged on creativity, technical skill, clarity, relevance to the competition's theme, and the ability to effectively communicate findings. Detailed judging criteria may vary each year.

faq.question: Is there an in-person event associated with the competition?
faq.answer: The competition often concludes with an in-person symposium or presentation event, where participants can showcase their work to a panel of judges, peers, and industry representatives.

faq.question: Do I need prior experience to participate?
faq.answer: No prior experience is necessary! The competition is designed to be inclusive, and participants can gain valuable skills throughout the process. Workshops and resources may also be provided to help you prepare.

faq.question: Are there any prizes for the competition?
faq.answer: Yes, prizes are usually awarded to winners in each category. These may include certificates, cash prizes, or other awards based on the competition's sponsorship and structure.

faq.question: How do I register for the competition?
faq.answer: Registration details are shared via club announcements, social media platforms, and emails. Keep an eye on these channels for deadlines and sign-up instructions.

faq.question: Can I work with a team?
faq.answer: Team participation is usually allowed and encouraged, though specific rules about team size and registration vary each year.

faq.question: What is the timeline for the competition?
faq.answer: The timeline varies each year but typically includes a registration period, project submission deadlines, judging phases, and a final presentation event. Be sure to check the official competition details for this year’s schedule.
